where: the lane's VM: timings after the first measurement
what: The same base binary measured 66 ms a body edit in its first run on the VM (07:16) and 260 to 370 ms in every run after (place 15 ms to 80-125, `memory purge` 5.6 ms to 96, CPU-bound spans 1.3 to 1.8 times longer), alone on the machine with fresh homes. `dd oflag=dsync` and file creates were as fast as before; `/proc/pressure/io` said 99% the whole time, with one idle daemon.
cost: every end-to-end row after the first is of a slow machine: the before and after here are compared as pairs run back to back, and the edit-loop rows are not comparable with other lanes'
cause: not found. The VM was made as the brief said, with no `--memory-commit` and no `--cpu` class; dmesg shows virtio-mem adding memory in 50 ms steps while two daemons ran; io pressure may be the daemons' io_uring waits counted as iowait
workaround: A/B back to back (`/root/ab.sh`), spans of CPU-bound stages, counts and bytes in place of wall time; then `ix restart edit4-1111`, after which the same binaries measured as in the first run (no-op build 12 ms, body edit 55 to 59 ms)
state: open: what slows a VM after an hour of builds and daemons is not found (a restart undoes it); a lane that measures edit loops should restart its VM before the rows, or have a benchmark VM (`--memory-commit`, a `--cpu` class)
